C1_shared_feedback_tuned_prior_homogeniz.statement: Feedback-tuned LLM co-writing reduces cross-author diversity more than solo and more than base LM assistance
C1_shared_feedback_tuned_prior_homogeniz.best_test: Padmakumar solo vs GPT-3 vs InstructGPT

support: GPT-3 does not reduce diversity vs solo (sharedness not = any assistance)
InstructGPT lower than solo in 60% of topics
Under InstructGPT, model spans less diverse than user spans
Under GPT-3, model spans more diverse than user spans (contrast)

caveats: InstructGPT lower than solo in 60% of topics only (not unanimous)
Does not prove cognitive offloading or debt; only output homogenization

evidence: CoAuthor: requesting suggestions associated with higher (not lower) cross-session diversity vs never-get (small never-get n)
CoAuthor: accept terciles nearly identical on group diversity
caveats: CoAuthor has no true solo control

C3_dose_response_more_acceptance_more_ho.statement: More suggestion acceptance causes more homogenization
evidence: CoAuthor: rank corr accept_rate vs sim_to_mean = +0.178 (mild support for individual atypicality loss)
CoAuthor: group diversity low vs high accept almost flat (0.929 vs 0.922)

C4_population_essays_became_less_diverse.statement: College essays became lexically/semantically less diverse after ChatGPT
evidence: OSF GU: post ChatGPT word_dist slightly HIGHER (refutes lexical homogenization at word level)
OSF GU: post document_dist slightly LOWER (weak support for embedding-level homogenization)
Observational year confound; ChatGPT label is pre/post era not individual AI use

C5_model_only_text_is_more_homogeneous_t.statement: Pure model generations are more homogeneous than human essays on same prompts
evidence: Matched within-prompt doc distance GPT 0.116 vs human 0.302
Within-subject: gpt_gen and gpt_revised lower document_dist than unaided essay
caveats: Shows model prior is narrow; does not by itself prove human co-writing converges cognitively

C6_cognitive_debt_transfer_loss_after_as.statement: LLM assistance causes worse later unaided / transfer performance
C6_cognitive_debt_transfer_loss_after_as.verdict: NOT TESTABLE with current public microdata we hold
evidence: Learning companion OSF: no unaided control arm
Kosmyna/Barcaui cited externally only; microdata closed

C7_cognitive_convergence_as_unified_mech.statement: Offloading onto a shared prior jointly explains homogenization AND debt
C7_cognitive_convergence_as_unified_mech.reason: Homogenization evidence (Padmakumar InstructGPT; pure GPT narrowness) does not identify offloading or debt. Debt not re-measured. CoAuthor and population word diversity do not cleanly confirm a general convergence story.

learning_corrected.what_data_is: Both study arms use ChatGPT as study companion (summary vs transcript; summary vs question). No no-AI control in released tables.
refute: Cannot attribute transfer debt to LLM vs unaided study: no unaided arm in processed tables
Condition mean differences on transfer are tiny (Study1: 7.91 vs 7.77; Study2: 6.48 vs 6.28) and not a shared-prior test
mixed: Within ChatGPT arms, help-count vs transfer correlations are mostly near zero; one arm shows positive corr (more help, better transfer)
Useful for interaction-style comparisons, not for cognitive-convergence claim
cannot_test: Homogenization not measurable (no multi-author text products comparable across people)
Transfer debt vs solo learning not identifiable here

keep: InstructGPT co-writing homogenizes relative to solo and GPT-3 in Padmakumar (H1-H3 hold there)
Model-only and GPT-revised text is narrower than unaided human essays (OSF yd94z)
drop_or_soften: Do not claim any assistance homogenizes; GPT-3 counterexample matters
Do not claim population lexical diversity collapsed post-ChatGPT; word_dist rose slightly
Do not claim transfer debt from our public learning data; design cannot identify it
Do not claim CoAuthor confirms homogenization; no solo arm and weak dose-response on group D
bottom_line.honest_paper_posture: Mechanism claim should be narrowed to: shared feedback-tuned priors can compress co-written output diversity. Broader cognitive-convergence / debt framing is a hypothesis, not a result we can defend with current public data.

support: GPT-3 does not reduce diversity vs solo (sharedness not = any assistance)
InstructGPT lower than solo in 60% of topics
Under InstructGPT, model spans less diverse than user spans
Under GPT-3, model spans more diverse than user spans (contrast)
Higher accept_rate associates with closer-to-mean text (rho=0.178)
refute: Sessions that requested suggestions MORE diverse than never-get
cannot_test: No unaided baseline: cannot test homogenization vs solo

support: Pure GPT essays much less within-prompt diverse than human (gpt=0.116 vs human=0.302)
gpt_gen_vs_essay: lower document_dist than unaided essay (delta=-0.1157, frac_lower=0.95)
gpt_revised_vs_essay: lower document_dist than unaided essay (delta=-0.0742, frac_lower=0.92)
refute: GU observational: post-ChatGPT word_dist HIGHER than pre (delta=0.0019)
mixed: Pure GPT vs human compares model-only text to humans; does not measure human+LLM co-writing homogenization
cannot_test: Pre/post ChatGPT is observational; year/cohort confounds; not proof of shared-prior mechanism
